introduction:
Registering a property in Maharashtra has become highly streamlined thanks to the state's digital initiatives. The process officially transfers the ownership of the property to your name, keeping you safe from legal disputes.

This guide provides a step-by-step, easy-to-understand walkthrough on how to complete your property registration from start to finish in Maharashtra.
quickFacts:
Important to Know
  • Governing Body: Inspector General of Registration and Stamps (IGR), Maharashtra.
  • Time Limit: By law, you must register the property within 4 months from the date the sale deed is signed (executed).
  • Stamp Duty Rates: Usually between 5% to 6% of the property's value (depending on city/municipal limits and Metro Cess).
  • Special Discount: Maharashtra offers a 1% stamp duty concession for women buyers purchasing residential real estate.
  • Registration Fee: 1% of the property value (strictly capped at a maximum of ₹30,000 for properties valued above ₹30 Lakhs).
documentsRequired:
Documents Required

Note: Keep the original and photocopies of the following documents ready before you begin registration.
Deeds & NOCs
  • The Sale Deed: The original drafted agreement signed by both the buyer and the seller.
  • NOC (No Objection Certificate): From the builder or the housing society, if applicable.
  • Chain Documents: Previous sale deeds showing the history of ownership.
Identity & Address Proofs
  • Identity Proofs: PAN Card and Aadhaar Card for the Buyer(s), Seller(s), and Two Witnesses.
  • Address Proofs: Passport, Voter ID, or recent utility bills for all parties.
  • Photographs: Passport-sized photographs of the buyer, seller, and both witnesses.
Property Records & Payments
  • Property Records: The 7/12 Extract (for land) or Property Card (for urban properties/apartments).
  • Payment Proofs: The e-challan or receipts proving payment of Stamp Duty and Registration Fees.
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Hybrid Online Data Entry & SRO Visit

Maharashtra uses a hybrid model called "e-filing" or "Public Data Entry (PDE)". You complete the details online from home and then visit the office briefly.

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Calculate Stamp Duty
    Visit the IGR Maharashtra portal to check the "Ready Reckoner Rate" (the government's minimum set price for properties in that area). Your stamp duty is calculated on whichever is higher: the Ready Reckoner Rate or your actual buying price.
  2. Pay Fees Online
    Go to the GRAS (Government Receipt Accounting System) portal. Enter your property details and pay the Stamp Duty and Registration Fee securely online via net banking or debit/credit card. Save and print the e-challan (payment receipt).
  3. Document Data Entry
    Go back to the IGR Maharashtra E-Filing system. Select "New User Registration", create an account, and fill in the details of the buyer, seller, and the property. Upload the drafted sale deed and payment receipts.
  4. Book an Appointment (e-Stepin)
    Once the data is entered, use the e-Stepin feature on the portal. Select your local Sub-Registrar Office (SRO), and pick a date and time slot for your physical SRO visit.
  5. The Offline Visit
    On the day of your appointment, the buyer, seller, and the two witnesses must physically go to the SRO with all original documents. Because you booked a slot online, you will not have to stand in a long queue.
  6. Biometric Verification
    At the SRO counter, an official will verify your physical documents. The buyer, seller, and witnesses will be asked to provide their fingerprints (biometrics) on a scanner and look into a webcam for live photographs.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Traditional Offline Registration

If you are uncomfortable with computers, you can still register your property traditionally, though it takes more time and standing in lines.

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Pay via Bank
    Instead of using the online GRAS portal, visit an authorized bank to pay your stamp duty and registration fees via a Demand Draft (DD) or Pay Order. The bank will issue you an e-SBTR (Electronic Secure Bank Treasury Receipt).
  2. Legal Drafting
    Hire a local lawyer or deed writer to physically draft your sale deed on standard non-judicial stamp paper.
  3. Walk-in to the SRO
    Take the buyer, seller, two witnesses, and all physical documents directly to the Sub-Registrar Office in the jurisdiction of your property.
  4. Queue and Submit
    Submit your documents manually to the registration clerk and wait for your turn to be called by the Sub-Registrar.
  5. Manual Processing
    You will physically sign the deed in front of the Sub-Registrar. Your biometrics (fingerprints and photos) will be captured digitally at the desk.
afterApplying:
After Registration — What Next?

Document Approval

The Sub-Registrar will officially record the transaction in the government logs.

Receiving Index II

You will be issued a highly crucial document called Index II. This is a 1-page summary of your transaction. Keep it incredibly safe, as it serves as the ultimate proof of registration.

Original Deed Retrieval

The digitally signed and registered Sale Deed will be handed back to you, or a link will be provided to download it online.

Crucial Final Step (Mutation)

Property registration does not automatically update the name on tax bills. You must submit a copy of your Index II and Sale Deed to the local Municipal Corporation (like BMC, PMC) or Tehsil office to get the tax records and 7/12 Extract transferred to your name.
